Closes a tunnel identified by the unique tunnel id. When a CloseTunnel request is received, we close the WebSocket connections between the client and proxy server so no data can be transmitted.

Requires permission to access the CloseTunnel action.
When set to true, IoT Secure Tunneling deletes the tunnel data immediately.
The ID of the tunnel to close.
The last time the connection status was updated.
The connection status of the tunnel. Valid values are CONNECTED and DISCONNECTED.
The state of a connection.

Gets information about a tunnel identified by the unique tunnel id.

Requires permission to access the DescribeTunnel action.
The tunnel to describe.
The tunnel being described.

A list of service names that identify the target application. The IoT client running on the destination device reads this value and uses it to look up a port or an IP address and a port. The IoT client instantiates the local proxy, which uses this information to connect to the destination application.
The name of the IoT thing to which you want to connect.
The destination configuration.

IoT Secure Tunneling

IoT Secure Tunneling creates remote connections to devices deployed in the field.

For more information about how IoT Secure Tunneling works, see IoT Secure Tunneling.

Endpoint.documentation: Override the endpoint used to send this request

Region.documentation: The AWS region used to dispatch the request.

UseDualStack.documentation: When true, use the dual-stack endpoint. If the configured endpoint does not support dual-stack, dispatching the request MAY return an error.

UseFIPS.documentation: When true, send this request to the FIPS-compliant regional endpoint. If the configured endpoint does not have a FIPS compliant endpoint, dispatching the request will return an error.

Thrown when an operation is attempted on a resource that does not exist.

Revokes the current client access token (CAT) and returns new CAT for clients to use when reconnecting to secure tunneling to access the same tunnel.

Requires permission to access the RotateTunnelAccessToken action.

Rotating the CAT doesn't extend the tunnel duration. For example, say the tunnel duration is 12 hours and the tunnel has already been open for 4 hours. When you rotate the access tokens, the new tokens that are generated can only be used for the remaining 8 hours.
